entertainment.title: Governors Awards: Glenn Close, Ridley Scott and Floyd Norman Accept Honorary Oscars, Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler Receive Thalberg Award
entertainment.summary: "I'm flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony," Ridley Scott said, referencing his late brother. "His great work would certainly have earned this recognition."
entertainment.body:
Five giants of the global film community were feted on Sunday night at the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences’ 17th annual Governors Awards : actress Glenn Close , animator Floyd Norman and — in absentia due to a recent medical procedure — director/producer Ridley Scott with bestowed honorary Oscars, and longtime indie producing partners Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler with the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award, which recognizes “creative producers whose bodies of work reflect a consistently high quality of motion picture production.”

The black-tie gathering, which took place inside the Ray Dolby Ballroom at Ovation Hollywood, was, as always, packed with Academy members — including most of the 55 members of the organization’s board of governors , who host the event — and dozens of current Oscar contenders. Among them: You Can See Everything ’s Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, The Odyssey ’s Christopher Nolan, Zendaya, Tom Holland and Charlize Theron, The Debut ’s Julianne Moore, Paul Giamatti and Emma Stone, Obsession ’s Curry Barker and Inde Navarrette, La Bola Negra ’s Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, Elsinore ’s Andrew Scott, The Invite ’s Olivia Wilde and Penélope Cruz, Wild Horse Nine ’s John Malkovich, Artificial ’s Andrew Garfield and Monica Barbaro, and Dune: Part Three ’s Timothée Chalamet, accompanied by Kylie Jenner. Related Stories TV Kids' Choice Awards: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners Movies 'Fatherland' Wins Top Camerimage Prize as 'Wild Horse Nine' Nabs Audience Award

Seated with Scott were his family, along with Lucy Fisher, Doug Wick, Jim Gianopulos, Tom Rothman, Richard Lovett, Simon Halls, Steve Asbell, Matt Damon and Jerry Bruckheimer, while Norman was notably joined by Marlon West and Travon Free. Close’s table consisted of Malkovich, Kevin Huvane, Franklin Latt, Rodrigo Garcia and Ram Bergman. Vachon and Koffler were accompanied by John Sloss, Wash Westmoreland, Marcus Hu and Liz Karlsen.

The first awardee was Norman, 91, who began his career in 1956 at Walt Disney Animation Studios as the company’s first Black animator. He contributed to numerous Disney classics including Sleeping Beauty , The Sword in the Stone , Mary Poppins , The Jungle Book and Robin Hood , as well as other notable films made outside of the Mouse House including The Hunchback of Notre Dame , Mulan , Monsters, Inc. and Toy Story 2 . A friend and mentor to younger animators and storyboard artists, he was the subject of a 2016 documentary feature, Floyd Norman: An Animated Life .

entertainment.title: Gracie Abrams Sets 2027 Australian Arena Shows for ‘Look at My Life Tour’
entertainment.summary: The singer-songwriter will play three nights each in Melbourne and Sydney next July and August, with Arlo Parks as a special guest
entertainment.body:
Gracie Abrams is bringing The Look at My Life Tour to Australia next year.

Abrams will play six arena shows across two cities in July and August 2027: three nights at Melbourne’s Rod Laver Arena on July 27, 28 and 30, followed by three at Sydney’s Afterpay Arena on Aug. 3, 4 and 6. British singer-songwriter Arlo Parks will open all six dates.

“Australia! I’ve missed you so much and I cannot express just how excited I am to return to Melbourne and Sydney next July/August for ‘The Look at My Life Tour,’” Abrams said in a statement. “A show that we’ve been working very hard to put together, a show that we hope you love as much as we do.” Related Daniel Hall, Co-Founder of Australian Rock Band Taxiride, Dies at 48 U2 Opens 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony With Surprise Performance Phil Collins Tells Rock Hall Crowd: 'You Haven't Heard the Last of Me' Explore Arlo Parks Gracie Abrams See latest videos, charts and news

“I’ve just missed you so much more than I can tell you… as soon as I heard for sure we were coming back my heart began to sing,” she added. “I will see you soon, I love you so much… we’re gonna make it great.”

The tour supports Daughter From Hell , Abrams’ third studio album, which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in July with 124,000 equivalent album units, her first chart-topping album. Produced with longtime collaborator Aaron Dessner, it also reached No. 1 in Australia. A deluxe edition arrives Friday (Nov. 20) with five additional tracks, including “Out of Nowhere,” which she first performed at Glastonbury in 2025, and “Crazy Girl,” previously available only on vinyl. The Look at My Life Tour launches Dec. 2 in Denver.

The run marks Abrams’ third visit to Australia in four years. She sold out six theater shows on her first trip in January 2024, then returned in 2025 for 11 arena dates across Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne, Adelaide and Perth on The Secret of Us Tour. This time she is concentrating on two markets.

The Secret of Us (2024) debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200, and its deluxe edition produced “That’s So True,” her first top 10 hit on the Billboard Hot 100. Her Taylor Swift collaboration “us.” earned a Grammy nomination for best pop duo/group performance. Abrams will also make her acting debut in the upcoming A24 film Please.

An artist presale begins Wednesday (Nov. 18) at 10 a.m. local time, followed by Frontier Touring and Live Nation presales Thursday (Nov. 19). General sale opens Friday (Nov. 20) at 10 a.m. local time.

The third concert that Karol G was set to perform on Sunday (Nov. 15) at the Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City, as part of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, has been postponed to Tuesday (Nov. 17) “due to health reasons of the artist,” Ocesa announced on social media.

entertainment.summary: Cynthia Nixon and Blake Ritson tell TVLine about the excitement (and challenges) involved with their new relationships on The Gilded Age.
entertainment.body:
HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "The Gilded Age" celebrated Peggy and William's nuptials on Sunday with an appropriately extravagant wedding, while two other intriguing relationships bloomed in the shadows.

Let's start with Ada and Dr. Reginald Harris (played by "24" star and car insurance aficionado Dennis Haysbert), one of William's professors from medical school. Ada's interaction with Dr. Harris at the wedding is brief, but there's a sweet, flirtatious energy to their meeting that begs to be explored — and explored it shall be.

"He's such a lovely man, and that voice, oh my God!" Cynthia Nixon tells TVLine. "He was our director Sally Richardson's idea. I think she wanted to give Ada someone that was really gorgeous, you know what I mean? Someone magnetic and so undeniable to really sweep her off her feet."

When Haysbert's casting in Season 4 was first announced by HBO, William's mentor was teased to be making a "surprising connection" during his time on the show, and that connection has now been revealed. Ada has always followed her heart, and she will continue to do so, but any potential courtship will certainly be tested by the societal stigma surrounding interracial relationships in the 1880s.

"Even though she has grown up and become more worldly as she has stepped into her wealth and position in the family, Ada still maintains that kind of girlish innocence," Nixon adds. "I think you have to be a little naive to keep walking forward with this relationship, trying to ignore what it would mean not only for you personally, but also for your family at large."

HBO Meanwhile, another romance is brewing between Oscar and Lee Klein (played by James Scully), the apprentice to famous artist William Merritt Chase. Like Ada and Dr. Harris, this new couple's first interaction is brief, but it's loaded with subtext. "Maybe I can persuade you to the merits of art," Lee tells Oscar when they meet at the van Rhijns' first salon, and Oscar says he's welcome to try.

Blake Ritson is choosing to celebrate his character's new romance, especially with the dark cloud that's been hanging over his head ever since the sudden death of John Adams last season .

"Having seen Oscar, in his own words, descending to the innermost circles of hell for two seasons, this rollercoaster just going steadily down, it's been fantastic [to have this new relationship]," Ritson tells TVLine. "I've loved this season where he's just on a really hedonistic run. He's canoodling and cocktailing and dancing."

entertainment.title: 10 Scrubs Episodes To Skip On A Rewatch
entertainment.summary: If you're planning to do a rewatch of "Scrubs," you don't have to make time for every single episode, as there are some that aren't worth revisiting.
entertainment.body:
NBC/ABC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Scrubs" is back, and, surprisingly, as great as it's ever been. There's no better time to check yourself back into Sacred Heart to relive how America's sweetest, funniest, and strangest medical dramedy first captured our hearts. The only thing that might stop you is the intimidating episode count — after all, a fair number of fans have certainly grown up and gone to med school since this first aired in the 2000s, and now only have time to sneak an episode or two in the on-call room.

Whatever the case, we've shaved your rewatch down significantly by surgically removing the benign (but largely unnecessary) episodes you don't need to see more than once. This includes all of Season 9 — which is, for better or for worse, no longer canon to the "Scrubs" story . In addition to those 13 episodes, we've found 10 more episodes from throughout the series' run that are safe to skip your second time around. These are narratively isolated stories that aren't classic or iconic enough within the fandom to demand your attention anyway. To be clear, they are by no means the show's worst episodes — in fact, making this list made us appreciate some of them a little more as interesting experiments and short films. They're just the episodes that won't make or break your rewatching experience.

NBC/ABC The most memorable thing about "My Own Personal Jesus" is that it's the first "Scrubs" Christmas episode. It's a must-watch around the holidays, but not essential for a rewatch. Structurally, it operates less like a traditional sitcom episode and more like a special with three equally weighted interwoven stories united by the idea of faith. It's hard to tell if it was intentionally written this way or if the episode's most emotionally leveraged plot doesn't stand out as much as it should.

On paper, it looks like a Turk-centric episode. Donald Faison's swaggering surgeon is shaken by a stretch of bad luck while on call at Sacred Heart — on Christmas Eve, no less. The amount of tragedy he experiences is enough to subvert his faith in God. It's an existential dilemma, certainly, but one that doesn't really hit with the impact of an A plot for two reasons. First, Turk's fateful night is imagined solely through a rewrite of "The 12 Days of Christmas." It gets the job done, but makes a big change very quickly. Second, despite Turk announcing that his faith is core to his identity at the top of this episode, it hasn't come up meaningfully until this point in the show, and it's only alluded to afterward. "My Own Personal Jesus" treats Turk's loss of faith like he's finding out Santa isn't real; it just kinda bums him out for the holidays. That's true of J.D.'s (Zach Braff) and Elliot's (Sarah Chalke) storylines as well.

entertainment.body:
CBS Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover A tragic twist on Sunday's episode of "Marshals" hits close to home for one series regular, whose painful personal experience inspired the heartbreaking storyline.

Season 2, Episode 6 of "Marshals" finds Kayce investigating the death of Mo's nephew Troy, whose passing is immediately written off as a suicide by a sheriff who'd rather not devote too many resources to a case from the reservation. While the sheriff believes Troy jumped from a cliff of his own accord, it's eventually uncovered that Troy had been arguing with someone who pushed him over the edge.

It's a tragic tale inspired by the death of 27-year-old Cole Brings Plenty , the real-life nephew of "Marshals" star Mo Brings Plenty. Cole previously appeared in two episodes of "Yellowstone" prequel "1923," playing Pete Plenty Clouds. Foul play was ruled out in Cole's death, but his family suspected otherwise.

"I was very thankful that [showrunner Spencer Hudnut] and the writers incorporated the storyline and the way they wrote it," Mo Brings Plenty tells TVLine. "My brother and I shared our real-life experiences with them and explained to them what occurred, and for them to take that and then create this beautiful storyline and give us, give me the opportunity to share that, I'm just so thankful."

CBS Mo Brings Plenty says that Troy's funeral scene was a particularly "personal" moment to film, not only because it recreated an authentic indigenous ceremony, but also because it reminded him of the emotional process his family endured saying goodbye to Cole.

"I remember during the funeral, when were giving my nephew Cole's body back to the grave site, one of our relatives was conducting it," the actor tells TVLine. "Even before we started, he said, 'They're going to show you that he's home safely.' He said, 'Look to the south,' so we looked to the south, and there was an eagle followed by a red-tailed hawk that flew down low by us. That was a good sense of relief, but also knowing that there are so many other families going through what we've experienced, we had to continue."

An even more poignant scene occurs in the episode's final moments as Mo says an additional private goodbye to his nephew. No words are spoken, but when Mo sees a white horse, a powerful — and somewhat bittersweet — sense of relief washes over him. The actor says it was important "to give space for Mo to have his own moment."

When the Oak Ridge Boys (Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Joe Bonsall , and Richard Sterban, who died Nov. 14 at 83) were inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2015, they brought with them some of the most recognizable — and singalong-ready — songs in the genre. From their first hit single, 1977’s “Y’all Come Back Saloon” to their version of “Elvira,” a 1981 crossover smash, the Oaks’ catalog is rich in country music gems. But they also had gospel music in their blood, working heavenly harmonies into secular hits like “Trying to Love Two Women” and releasing full albums of gospel material throughout their decades-long career. Here are 10 of the vocal quartet’s must-hear songs.

The Oak Ridge Boys got their start in the 1940s, when they came out of Knoxville, Tennessee, singing gospel as the Oak Ridge Quintet, and they kept the classic vocal group tradition alive when they went country in the slick 1970s and 1980s. The Oaks’ casual-sharp look and equally pliant musical outlook made their crossover moves feel easy, including appearances on other artists’ tunes (like their beautiful low-key turn on Paul Simon’s “Slip Slidin’ Away”). Their biggest pop moment was “Elvira,” with its jovial gait, horn section, and fun-to-sing hook “Giddy up, um-poppa-um-poppa, mow, mow,” delivered by well-deep bass singer and Camden, New Jersey, native Richard Sterban. (Oaks tenor Joe Bonsall was born just across the Delaware River in Philadelphia.) — J.D.

entertainment.title: Gene Siskel And Roger Ebert Reviewed Just One Television Show
entertainment.summary: Throughout their many years on the air, Siskel and Ebert held back their opinions on TV ... except for this particular project starring an SNL alumnus.
entertainment.body:
The forgotten '90s sitcom hit rather close to home for Ebert and Siskel. The series followed the life of Jay Sherman, an elitist movie critic who ruthlessly panned the latest ridiculous films cranked out of Hollywood. Former "Saturday Night Live" star Jon Lovitz voiced the New York City-based critic as he took down spoofs of popular films such as "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids" and "The Terminator," amongst others. When he wasn't reviewing blockbusters on his show, Jay had more than enough to deal with at home with his son, Marty (Christine Cavanaugh), his eccentric adoptive parents (Gerrit Graham and Judith Ivey), and his clumsy love life.

Though the sitcom satirized critics like Ebert and Siskel, they appreciated the show's humor and had many good things to say about it... along with some constructive feedback.

Fox In a review of the sitcom, Gene Siskel said the first episode was "very funny," noting the movie spoofs were the show's strongest point.

"If 'The Critic' is going to succeed — and I hope it does — it definitely needs to refocus itself on the movies," Siskel said. "The show needs two things: A second critic, and Roger and me to write some of the scripts. We could save this show, and I, for one, would like to."

The critics felt that, besides Jon Lovitz's Jay Sherman, the show lacked a cast of "memorable characters" and advised against focusing too much on Jay's personal life to avoid becoming just "another sitcom." But Roger Ebert praised the show in his own review , writing that it does a good job of humanizing the role of a film critic through Jay. "It is impossible not to like this guy," he wrote.

Ebert and Siskel later appeared as themselves in the Season 2 episode "Siskel & Ebert & Jay & Alice" that highlighted their iconic partnership. The show has since been remembered as one of the best animated sitcoms ever made after it premiered on ABC in 1994, but it was unfortunately canceled after it moved to the Fox network for its second season.

entertainment.title: Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys’ Bass Singer, Dead at 83
entertainment.summary: Sterban's baritone delivery of "oom poppa mow-mow" in "Elvira" helped give the Country Music Hall of Fame vocal group its signature song
entertainment.body:
Richard Sterban , the bass vocalist whose river-deep delivery of “oom poppa mow-mow” in the crossover hit “Elvira” helped give the Oak Ridge Boys their signature song, died Saturday. He was 83. Sterban’s rep, Jeremy Westby, confirmed the singer’s death, adding that the Country Music Hall of Fame member died “due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia.” In March, Sterban said that he had been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer.

A native of Collingswood, New Jersey, Sterban grew up across the Delaware River from his future Oak Ridge Boys bandmate, the Philadelphia-born Joe Bonsall . But the pair first crossed paths in the gospel music community, in the quartet the Keystones, which Sterban helped form.

Gospel music defined Sterban’s early years and put him in the circle of rock & roll royalty when he joined J.D. Sumner and the Stamps near the end of the Sixties and hit the road with the group behind Elvis Presley in 1971. Sterban toured with Presley until 1972 when he left to join the Oak Ridge Boys, but his time with “The King of Rock & Roll” was deeply impactful: In the 1972 doc Elvis on Tour , Sterban, fellow bass singer Sumner, and the Stamps are seen harmonizing backstage with Presley on the gospel standard “Bosom of Abraham.” He’d go on to detail his history with Presley in the 2012 memoir From Elvis to Elvira: My Life On Stage .

Prior to becoming country music stars, the Oak Ridge Boys — like both the Keystones and the Stamps — were primarily a gospel group. The outfit started as the Oak Ridge Quartet and cycled through numerous members before landing on the most well-known lineup of William Lee Golden, Duane Allen, Sterban, and Bonsall. In 1974, they released their self-titled album, but it was 1977’s Y’all Come Back Saloon and its title track that put them on the country music charts. (They were already on the radar of Paul Simon: In 1976, the songwriter recruited the Oaks to sing backup on his song “Slip Slidin’ Away.”) Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

A string of successful albums and singles followed — a version of Rodney Crowell’s “Leaving Louisiana in the Broad Daylight,” the Number One hit “Trying to Love Two Women” — leading up to the album that would turn them into radio hitmakers, 1981’s Fancy Free . The LP was a country music smash and went on to be certified double platinum, thanks to songs like the title track “(I’m Settin’) Fancy Free” and the crossover juggernaut “Elvira.”

entertainment.title: 5 Once-Beloved '90s Sitcoms That Nobody Talks About Anymore
entertainment.summary: There was a lot more to network sitcoms in the '90s than Seinfeld and Friends. Here are some of the half-hour comedies that go underdiscussed.
entertainment.body:
MovieStillsDB Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover There's a real argument that the '90s should be considered the golden era for sitcoms. It's when they began stepping outside the living room –- both in setting and subject matter –- and into the world. The best sitcoms of the '90s not only continued to showcase stellar casts and writers, but they challenged conventions and pushed the envelope in satire, representation, technical artistry, and cultural commentary. As a result, many sitcoms of that decade stand the test of time.

But one inevitable consequence of having almost too many great options to talk about is that some will be forgotten. There are plenty of '90s sitcoms that had strong multi-season runs with devoted followings but have ultimately slipped from today's pop cultural conversations. Whether dated references cause a show to get left behind or limited streaming options make it hard for viewers to discover or rediscover it, it's not easy for sitcoms to stay relevant. Not every show can be like "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air," or any other '90s sitcom that gets better on rewatch . But, as TV continues to move forward, there's still space for one or two (or five) nostalgic shout-outs. Here are five previously loved '90s sitcoms that aren't talked about anymore.

NBC Four aliens come to Earth on a mission to study humans. Over time, they grow to appreciate humanity, while also becoming a real (odd) family. Though the premise wasn't 100% original (it was often compared to "Mork & Mindy"), "3rd Rock from the Sun" struck a chord with audiences at the time due to its unique blend of sci-fi, old-school slapstick, and mid-'90s weirdness. The ensemble cast was led by a theatrical John Lithgow as alien mission commander Dick Solomon. He and Kristen Johnston, who played Dick's sister Sally Solomon, earned a total of five Primetime Emmy Awards between them for their performances.

Harry Solomon (French Stewart), the oddball "uncle" of the crew, and Tommy Solomon (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), the oldest alien posing as a teenager, were standouts as well. Tommy was Gordon-Levitt's breakout TV role, which launched him into tween stardom. As sitcoms of the '00s — such as in "The Office" and "The Big Bang Theory" — would fully embrace awkward characters and situations, "3rd Rock from the Sun" can be seen as an early taste of that flavor.

In a 1997 interview with the LA Times , Stewart described how the cast leaned into their quirky roles. "It's closer to theater," he said. "It's just farce. So it sort of enables us to pump it up and chew scenery, you know, to just really go nuts. And I think from the very beginning, Mr. Lithgow set the pace."

entertainment.title: 10 Most Underrated Marvel Cartoons Of All Time
entertainment.summary: Over the decades, several Marvel cartoons have entertained superhero fans, and some of the best ones might have flown under your radar.
entertainment.body:
Disney Channel Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Boasting some of the most recognizable superheroes in the world, Marvel Comics has had its characters adapted into animated television shows for over 60 years. Some of the best superhero TV shows of all time , in any medium, are based on Marvel properties. But with decades' worth of Marvel cartoons, there are some that aren't as fondly remembered as they deserve. With that in mind, we're highlighting the animated Marvel superhero series that should get wider and more positive recognition.

Whether it's some of the many Spider-Man or X-Men shows or more obscure Marvel properties, these cartoons have gone severely overlooked. Some of these shows are unfairly compared to more celebrated predecessors or suffered from short runs. What all these series have in common is that they're all worth checking out regardless of their relative obscurity. These are the 10 most underrated Marvel cartoons of all time, each worthy of a revisit and reappraisal.

Nicktoons Given that Iron Man became the face of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, at least initially, the Iron Avenger received his own animated series shortly after the MCU's launch. Debuting in 2009, "Iron Man: Armored Adventures" follows a younger version of Tony Stark (Adrian Petriw), who builds his first super-powered armor after his father's apparent death. While investigating what became of his dad, Tony tangles with Obadiah Stane (Mackenzie Gray) and the Mandarin (Vincent Tong). The second and final season aligns the show closer to the movie "Iron Man 2," including the introductions of Black Widow (Ashleigh Ball) and Justin Hammer (Michael Adamthwaite).

With its use of cel-shaded computer-generated animation, "Iron Man: Armored Adventures" is one of the most visually impressive Iron Man-centric shows. But more than just with its presentation, the show really digs into the rivalry between Iron Man and the Mandarin on a more personal level than prior depictions. The second season also organically expands the narrative scope, making Tony a bigger part of the Marvel Universe. The best animated series starring Iron Man to date, "Iron Man: Armored Adventures" finds a fresh approach to its superhero's mythos.

Nicktoons Wolverine has grown into something of the face of the X-Men, both in terms of movies and video games. The 2009 animated series "Wolverine and the X-Men" similarly puts the clawed mutant center stage, as evidenced right in its title. The story begins with Wolverine (Steve Blum) and Beast (Fred Tatasciore) reforming the X-Men after the team disbanded following an attack on the X-Mansion. However, just as the show began to gain its creative momentum, it was canceled after a single season.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs in Hall of Fame company with a long list of statistical achievements
sports.summary: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had another phenomenal game on Sunday, and in his fourth NFL season he has hit a long list of statistical milestones that only Hall of Famers have reached before him.
sports.body:
In Sunday’s 35-10 win over the Patriots, Gibbs carried 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns, and added seven catches for 99 yards. After the game, the NFL distributed a list of Gibbs’ stats that show him either equaling or exceeding the accomplishments of some of the greatest running backs ever to play the game. Among Gibbs’ milestones:

Gibbs has the most touchdowns in NFL history in a player’s first four seasons. He has now scored 62 touchdowns (50 rushing and 12 receiving), breaking the previous record of Hall of Famer Terrell Davis, who had 61 touchdowns in his first four seasons.

Gibbs’ 50 career rushing touchdowns make him the third player in NFL history to run for 50 touchdowns before turning 25. The other two are Hall of Famers Barry Sanders with 52, and Emmitt Smith with 50. Gibbs doesn’t turn 25 until after this season, so he’s a near-lock to move ahead of Sanders and into first place on the all-time list.

Gibbs and Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson are the only players in NFL history to have multiple games with at least 250 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns before turning 25.

Gibbs, Tomlinson and Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson are the only players to have four games of at least 200 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in their first four seasons.

Gibbs has topped 1,200 scrimmage yards and 10 rushing touchdowns in each of his first four seasons. The only players who have done that before are Tomlinson, Dickerson, Hall of Famer Earl Campbell and future Hall of Famer Adrian Peterson.

Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown have played 24 games together in which they’ve both scored touchdowns, surpassing Bills Hall of Famers Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed, who both scored in 23 games, for the fourth-most games in which running back-wide receiver teammates both score. All the players ahead of Gibbs and St. Brown are Hall of Famers: Emmitt Smith and Michael Irvin did it 32 times for the Cowboys, Lenny Moore and Raymond Berry did it 31 times for the Colts, and Edgerrin James and Marvin Harrison did it 25 times for the Colts.

Only three and a half seasons into his NFL career, it’s too early to put Gibbs in the Hall of Fame. But everything about the way he has played so far indicates that some day he’ll have a bust in Canton.

sports.title: Mike McCarthy: "That's clearly not to the standard of the Pittsburgh Steelers"
sports.summary: "I was very disappointed. We're all disappointed," McCarthy said after a 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
sports.body:
“That’s clearly not to the standard of the Pittsburgh Steelers. It’s not to any of our expectations,” McCarthy said. “I was very disappointed. We’re all disappointed.”

Heading into the game, the Steelers and Bengals were tied atop the AFC North at 6-2. Now the Bengals have a one-game lead and currently would have the tiebreaker edge over the Steelers as well. The Bengals are now the overwhelming betting favorites to win the division at -600, with the Steelers far behind at +700.

But as badly as McCarthy’s team played, he said he can’t overreact to one game.

“It’s one loss and it will be dealt with,” McCarthy said. “I’m more focused on the details, the fundamentals, and the things we need to do. We’re not gonna drive down the drama road of those types of things. It’s a waste of time, it’s a waste of energy. We’re going to pour our energy into ourselves, looking in the mirror and focusing on the things we can control.”

The Steelers were not even competitive on Sunday night, and now it’s time for McCarthy to search for answers.

In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 - 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 - 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it’s possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. sports.title: Sunday Night Football: Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase torch Steelers in 38-18 Bengals victory
sports.summary: Burrow threw for 409 yards and four TDs while Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards.
sports.body:
After the performance against the Steelers, they may want to make that alternate kit permanent.

Quarterback Joe Burrow and receiver Ja’Marr Chase were stellar on Sunday night, with Cincinnati defeating division-rival Pittsburgh 38-18.

In just the first half, Burrow had 302 yards and three touchdowns before finishing the contest 35-of-44 for 409 yards with four TDs. Joe Flacco came in for mop-up duty midway through the final period.

Burrow also tied Peyton Manning’s record streak of five consecutive games of at least four touchdowns .

As he often is, Chase was Burrow’s favorite target, catching 11 passes for 231 yards. While Chase didn’t have a touchdown himself, he caught deep bombs of 53 and 43 yards that helped set up scores.

It was the third-highest output of Chase’s career and the fourth time he’s gone over 200 yards in a regular-season game.

The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions, and would have made it all five if Evan McPherson had hit his 43-yard field goal attempt that sailed wide right. That was McPherson’s first missed kick of the season.

But McPherson had opened the scoring with a 24-yard field goal to cap the opening drive. Drew Sample had a 3-yard TD catch, Chase Brown had a 2-yard score, and Dohnte Meyers had a 15-yard touchdown reception to give the Bengals a 24-3 halftime lead.

sports.title: Joe Burrow matches Peyton Manning's record for consecutive games with at least four TDs
sports.summary: Joe Burrow has accomplished something that had not been done for over 20 years.
sports.body:
With his 4-yard touchdown to Chase Brown in the third quarter, Burrow became the first since Peyton Manning in 2004 to have at least four total touchdowns in five consecutive games, which is the longest streak in NFL history.

That score gave the Bengals a commanding 31-3 lead with 4:12 left in the third period.

Burrow has been excellent all season, but that’s particularly been the case on Sunday night. So far, he’s completed 32-of-41 passes for 359 yards with four TDs.

The one difference between Manning’s streak and Burrow’s is that Manning did it with all passing touchdowns. Between Weeks 8 and 12 in 2004, Manning threw for five, four, five, four, and six TDs with the Colts.

Burrow has thrown for four, four, five, three, and now four in his last six games. He’s also had a rushing touchdown in each of the last two weeks before Sunday’s matchup against Pittsburgh.

sports.title: Sunday Night Football: Joe Burrow torching Steelers, Bengals lead 24-3 at halftime
sports.summary: Burrow threw for 302 yards and three touchdowns in the first half.
sports.body:
Cincinnati’s quarterback threw for 302 yards and three touchdowns in the first two quarters as the Bengals have a 24-3 lead at halftime.

Burrow completed 26-of-34 passes in the first half. Seven completions went to Ja’Marr Chase for 146 yards, including a 53-yard downfield pass. Tee Higgins — who went back to the locker room just before the half for an injury check — caught five passes for 66 yards.

Cincinnati scored on a 24-yard field goal to cap an opening drive, then used a 13-play, 92-yard drive to make the score 10-0 with Burrow’s 3-yard touchdown to Drew Sample. Chase Brown then caught a 2-yard touchdown pass to make the score 17-0.

After Chris Boswell put the Steelers on the board with a 45-yard field goal late in the second period, the Bengals got right down the field and scored on Burrow’s 15-yard pass to Dohnte Meyers.

The only thing that stopped Cincinnati’s offense in the first half was kicker Evan McPherson, who missed his first kick of the season in sending a 43-yard field goal attempt wide right in the second quarter.

Cincinnati’s defense has played just as well as its offense. Pittsburgh was limited to just four first downs and 40 total yards in the first half. Aaron Rodgers started the game 0-of-8 passing, finishing the half 4-of-12 for 25 yards.

Rodgers had never started a game 0-of-8 in his career, according to the NBC broadcast. His first completion was a 5-yard pass to Darnell Washington with 4:31 left in the second quarter.

Pittsburgh will get a shot to turn it around to start the third quarter, as the team will receive the second-half kickoff.

sports.title: Dak Prescott: 49ers fans "were more present than ours"
sports.summary: On Sunday, America's Team wasn't even Dallas's Team. 49ers fans showed up in big numbers for the game against the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.
sports.body:
After the game, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott was asked whether the home team had to use the silent count.

“No, we didn’t go on the silent count,” Prescott said. "[We] anticipated it. I think y’all even potentially asked me on Thursday about it, having this many 49er fans there. Tricked myself and told myself early on that the red was for my high school.

“And at the end of the day, all I asked for is a great environment to play this game. And unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours, but it created a great atmosphere. So, we take the good out of it one way or another.”

For owner Jerry Jones, the colors worn by the fans don’t matter; their money is the same shade of green.

Still, it’s always a bad look when too many fans of the opposing team show up for a road game. On Sunday, 49ers fans found their way to buy tickets and infiltrate the venue.

And their fans got to see the Niners move to 8-1 on the season.

sports.title: Carson Beck on his first start: It was cool, but losing is awful
sports.summary: Carson Beck started his first NFL game Sunday.
sports.body:
“The ebbs and flows of football, I’ve been through it ,” Beck said, via Darren Urban of the team website. “Not at this level. But it’s still the same game that we play. I’ve been through the good, the bad, the ugly, the uglier.

“How are you able to respond when things go bad? Obviously, we didn’t respond well today, and that starts with me. . . . But having the opportunity to play, that’s what allows us to stay focused. To be out there is fun. Football is fun.”

Beck went 11-of-18 for 108 yards and two interceptions in the 34-6 loss to the Rams. The Cardinals had only 123 yards and six first downs.

Coach Mike LaFleur said Beck did everything they asked him to do but conceded it was “a rough day” for the offense.

“It was cool,” Beck said. “Losing is awful. Don’t get it twisted. Losing is the worst thing ever. I hate losing. I haven’t done a lot of it. But it’s not about me. It’s about the team, and what we can do to fix the things to win games like this.

“But it was awesome. Going out on the first drive, looking across the field at guys like Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. I just smiled for a second and was like, ‘This is sick.’ This is the thing you dream of when you start playing football at 6, 7 years old.”

sports.title: Christian McCaffrey on career-high receiving yards: You just catch it and run as fast as you can
sports.summary: Christian McCaffrey had a day.
sports.body:
The 49ers running back had never had more than 121 receiving yards in a single game. He had 161 receiving yards on four catches Sunday against the Cowboys, scoring on catch-and-runs of 74 and 66 in the 49ers’ 46-40 win.

“You never know,” McCaffrey said. “You go into each game. You don’t really predict anything. Again, you just have to have the right mindset on a play that’s going to break. You trust your instincts and play fast.”

His first receiving touchdown came when Brock Purdy rolled to his right to buy time and found McCaffrey running free on the scramble drill.

“It really is backyard football at that point,” McCaffrey said. “We all played it as kids at recess, and you draw up plays on your hand, and it never happens. You ever tell a 5-year-old to run a post route, and he just runs a corner and something else, but he’s open? That’s kind of what that was. Again, I think those little decisions that you make in games, from Brock to scramble, not to just surrender the play but to keep it alive. That’s a big deal. There’s no planning that goes into that. It’s just him doing a great job playing ball.”

What turned out to be the game-winning touchdown came with 3:23 remaining when Purdy found McCaffrey, who was matched up against Von Miller, over the middle.

“They brought pressure,” McCaffrey said. “They dropped a D-end on me, so that’s a perfect look for that play. Again, it was a great job by Brock getting the ball where it needed to be. It made it easy for me.

“You just catch it and run as fast as you can to try to score. Don’t overthink it. You hope that nobody catches you, and you hope that you’re really fast so your teammates don’t catch up to you to celebrate, because it makes you look slow. We’ll have to check the tape.”

McCaffrey had a 16-yard touchdown run and 62 yards rushing. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown.

sports.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should be taken seriously as an MVP candidate
sports.summary: No player as been more valuable to his team this year than JSN.
sports.body:
And, frankly, Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba should be taken very seriously as an MVP candidate.

Sure, no receiver has ever won the NFL MVP award. No receiver has ever done what he’s doing, either.

With 171 yards and a touchdown on Sunday against the Raiders, Smith-Njigba has 1,206 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns through 10 games. No one has done that since 1960.

Think about that. Think of all the great receivers who have played since the NFL relaxed the rules to promote more passing. Even then, only three players had ever gotten to 1,200 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns in 10 games before today: Don Hutson in 1942, Elroy “Crazy Legs” Hirsch in 1951, and Raymond Berry in 1960.

Smith-Njigba remains on pace to set the new single-season receiving yardage record. And to become the first player in league history with 2,000 or more receiving yards in a season.

Often, a receiver who has a special season loses MVP votes to the quarterback who fed him the passes. With the Seahawks using both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock, neither will be taking MVP votes away from anyone.

Then there’s the official definition of MVP: “The player who was most valuable to their team over the course of the season.” Smith-Njigba accounts for more than half of the Seattle passing offense. Even when everyone knows the ball is coming to him, he still makes plays.

For now, those inclined to wager on the MVP winner haven’t taken JSN seriously. His odds to win the award are 80-1.

sports.title: Christian McCaffrey, 49ers run past Cowboys 46-40
sports.summary: The 49ers had 584 yards, the third-most the Cowboys have allowed in their history.
sports.body:
In an entertaining game, the 49ers moved to 8-1, and the Cowboys fell to 4-6.

Christian McCaffrey had a career-high 161 receiving yards on four catches, two of them touchdowns, and ran for 62 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown.

The 49ers led 38-19 with 11:26 remaining in the fourth quarter. But George Pickens caught a 5-yard touchdown pass, which was followed by a missed 2-point conversion. Ryan Flournoy’s 11-yard score with 3:42 left cut the Cowboys’ deficit to 38-32. The 49ers burned only 2:26 on their possession in between, punting after four plays.

The 49ers showed the Cowboys who they are, though, when Brock Purdy hit McCaffrey across the middle of the field. Von Miller, who was covering McCaffrey, and his teammates had no chance of catching the running back, who went 66 yards to the end zone.

The Cowboys didn’t go away quietly, scoring once more on CeeDee Lamb’s 1-yard reception. Dak Prescott ran in the 2-point conversion.

Dallas tried an onside kick despite having three timeouts and did not convert.

Kaelon Black, who had 11 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled on the second-down play. Quinnen Williams forced it, but Black was able to get back on the ball. The 49ers punted, and the Cowboys were left with only 9 seconds and in need of 91 yards and a miracle.

McCaffrey’s other touchdowns were a 74-yard reception and a 16-yard run.

sports.title: Seahawks shut down Raiders in second half of 21-13 win
sports.summary: The Raiders led 10-7 at halftime, but the Seahawks took over in the final 30 minutes.
sports.body:
Mendoza ran for a touchdown to open the game helped the Raiders to a 10-7 lead over the defending champions through 30 minutes of play in Las Vegas. The second half was a very different story, however.

The Raiders were shut out until a Matt Gay field goal with 2:04 left to play in the game and the Seahawks scored a pair of touchdowns to pick up a 21-13 win. The victory pushes their record to 6-4 as they head into their bye week and it came after one of the smartest special teams plays we’re likely to see this season.

After Gay’s field goal, Seahawks returner Tory Horton jumped to bat the ensuing kickoff back in bounds rather than let it sail out for a touchback. He also had the presence of mind to tell Rashid Shaheed to return the ball since he stepped out of bounds and couldn’t do it himself. The play wound up taking the clock through the two-minute warning, which meant the Raiders could only stop the clock twice rather than three times.

The Seahawks only ran 17 offensive plays in the first half of the game, but they found their footing behind Zach Charbonnet and Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the second half. Charbonnet ran 12 times for 55 yards and Smith-Njigba continued his remarkable season with seven catches for 160 yards after the break. One of those was a 71-yard touchdown from Drew Lock.

All in all, Seattle picked up 274 yards in the final two quarters while holding the Raiders to 27 yards on their final six possessions. They sacked Mendoza four times in the second half and the loss of tight end Brock Bowers to an ankle injury left the rookie without real options in the passing game.

Mendoza, who finished 17-of-29 for 143 yards, will now try for his first win in Denver next weekend.

sports.title: Rams roll to 34-6 victory over Cardinals
sports.summary: After winning four in a row, Los Angeles heads into a Week 11 bye at 6-4.
sports.body:
But Los Angeles got going late in the second quarter and went on to roll to a 34-6 blowout victory.

The Rams have now won four in a row after starting the season 2-4, with their last loss coming on Oct. 18 to the Cardinals at home.

Starting late in the second quarter, the Rams scored four consecutive touchdowns to make the game a laugher. Quarterback Matthew Stafford hit Tyler Higbee with a 5-yard touchdown to get things started with just over a minute left in the second period. Then after a Kam Kinchens interception, Stafford connected with Xavier Smith for a 22-yard touchdown on a screen pass to give L.A. a 17-6 halftime lead.

Blake Corum kept the roll going to open the second half, scoring on a 1-yard run. Then Stafford hit Davis Allen for a 19-yard TD to make the score 31-6 with 5:55 left.

Brandon McManus closed out the scoring with a 43-yard field goal.

The Rams finished the game holding the ball for the final 12:15 of the contest, with Ronnie Rivers getting 81 yards on 15 carries to close it out.

L.A. ended the game leading time of possession 42:23 to 17:37. The Rams had 28 first downs, 436 total yards, and were 7-of-12 on third down. Arizona had just six first downs, 123 total yards, and the team was 0-of-6 on third down.

Corum led Los Angeles with 100 yards on 17 carries with a touchdown. He also caught three passes for 19 yards.

sports.title: Deebo Samuel's 70-yard TD run gives 49ers 31-19 lead
sports.summary: Welcome back, Deebo Samuel.
sports.body:
The wide receiver, who hadn’t played since Oct. 11, scored his second touchdown. His first came on an 11-yard reception. His second came on a reverse.

Quarterback Brock Purdy flipped to Kaelon Black, who was running right, and the running back flipped it to Samuel running left. Trent Williams and Purdy were among the caravan of blockers Samuel had in front of him.

The 49ers lead 31-19 with 6:59 remaining in the third quarter.

Samuel has three carries for 78 yards and two catches for 22 yards.

The Cowboys also allowed Christian McCaffrey to score on a 74-yard catch-and-run in the first half.

It is the 17th consecutive game the Cowboys have allowed at least 20 points.

sports.title: Carucci Take 2: Bills reinforce elite status with ‘best win’ of the season
sports.summary: “I think this is the best win we’ve had this season,” said Joe Brady, the NFL’s first head coach to go 8-1 since Minnesota’s Kevin O’Connell in 2022.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills ground New York Jets, improve to 8-1 with Week 10 win
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills earned their first AFC East divisional win this season thanks to a persistent attack that gradually wore down an overmatched New York Jets team in all three phases of the game. The Bills were once again held in check until halftime, but the offense came out with an aggressive swagg
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills earned their first AFC East divisional win this season thanks to a persistent attack that gradually wore down an overmatched New York Jets team in all three phases of the game. The Bills were once again held in check until halftime, but the offense came out with an aggressive swagger after the break that broke most of the Jets’ prior momentum. You might say that head coach Joe Brady has put together a masterclass in his first season at the helm, lulling opponents into a false sense of hope through the first two quarters, only to pull the rug out from under them when it counts. Buffalo again started the game on offense, thanks to another lost coin toss. It didn’t work out as Brady probably planned for in New Jersey, though the choice wasn’t his to make this weekend. The Jets’ forced a punt that soon ushered in a mid-tempo battle in the trenches for the duration of the half. The Bills eventually found the end zone in the first quarter thanks to another goal-line carry by Allen. The Jets’ defense caused plenty of early confusion and frustration for Allen and the passing game, ultimately holding them to just 10 points at halftime. Thankfully, Buffalo’s defense was ready for a slugfest and limited the Jets to just two field goals through two quarters while having to defend two different quarterbacks in starter Geno Smith (who was injured before the break), and rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik. If you caught his quick interview after the half, it was clear Brady was annoyed at his mostly stagnant first-half offense. They responded to what must have been an epic challenge speech in the locker room, which led to three second-half touchdowns and a 31-12 blowout win. A defense that’s been ranked as low as last and currently resides in the middle of the pack held an under-the-radar and (yes) talented Jets offense out of the end zone. These are the sorts of building blocks that matter when it comes to postseason discussions. The Bills can’t control their schedule or who suits up, but in watching the defense it’s clear things have begun to click and they’re responding far better to in-game adversity. It was a banner day for the pass rush, which claimed four more sacks. The unit was led by rookie edge rusher T.J. Parker, who notched a pair to increase his total to three on the season. sports.title: Blake Corum scores for sixth consecutive game, Rams lead 24-6
sports.summary: Blake Corum won't stop scoring, and the Rams have increased their lead early in the second half.
sports.body:
Corum’s 1-yard touchdown run gave the Rams a 24-6 lead in the third quarter.

It’s the sixth consecutive game with a touchdown for Corum, who now has five rushing TDs and six total touchdowns on the season.

With Los Angeles’ offense missing several key players, Corum leads with 67 yards on 12 carries. He also has three catches for 19 yards.

L.A. has now scored touchdowns on three consecutive possessions to take control of the game.

On the injury front, Cardinals linebacker Jordan Burch (knee), Rams center Coleman Shelton (hamstring), and Rams backup center Dylan McMahon (knee) have all been ruled out.

sports.title: 49ers lead Cowboys 17-16 at halftime
sports.summary: The 49ers and Cowboys are in a shootout at AT&T Stadium.
sports.body:
In an entertaining first half, the difference is an extra point. Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed one, giving the 49ers a 17-16 halftime lead.

Christian McCaffrey scored on a 74-yard catch-and-run touchdown after Brock Purdy rolled to his right to buy time. Eddy Pineiro’s PAT gave San Francisco a lead with 2:26 remaining in the first half.

The 49ers’ other points came on Deebo Samuel’s 11-yard touchdown catch and Pineiro’s 28-yard field goal.

The 49ers outgained the Cowboys 244 to 165, with Purdy going 12-of-17 for 217 yards and two touchdowns. McCaffrey has two catches for 81 yards and a touchdown and eight rushes for 21 yards.

The 49ers can’t cover George Pickens, who returned from a one-game absence with a hamstring injury and has touchdowns of 35 and 39 yards. He has six catches for 97 yards.

Dak Prescott is 7-for-17 for 104 yards and two touchdowns, with Ryan Flournoy having the only other catch besides Pickens’ six.

Aubrey kicked a 52-yard field goal on the team’s first drive.

sports.title: Jadarian Price puts Seahawks up 14-10 in third quarter
sports.summary: Fernando Mendoza isn't the only rookie who has scored his first NFL touchdown in Las Vegas on Sunday.
sports.body:
Seahawks running back Jadarian Price went far later in the first round than Mendoza, but he also found his way into the end zone on Sunday. Price’s 12-yard run put the Seahawks up over the Raiders 14-10 with 9:28 to play in the third quarter.

Price’s touchdown capped a drive that saw Drew Lock hook up with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba twice for 53 yards. Smith-Njigba only had one catch in the first half and the Seahawks had five first downs on the drive after picking up four of them in the first 30 minutes.

The change in offensive fortunes for the Seahawks means Mendoza will need to mount a comeback to get a win in his first NFL start.

sports.title: Matthew Stafford throws two TD passes, Rams lead Cardinals 17-6 at halftime
sports.summary: The Rams have more injury issues to deal with on offense.
sports.body:
Matthew Stafford tossed a 5-yard touchdown pass to Tyler Higbee to cap a 10-play, 72-yard drive late in the second quarter.

Then rookie Carson Beck threw a tough-luck interception, as Devin Duvernay dropped a pass that went right to him and defensive back Kam Kinchens came away with the pass — returning it to Arizona’s 32-yard line.

A few plays later, Stafford connected with Xavier Smith on a screen for a 22-yard touchdown, putting the Rams up by 11.

With top pass catchers out, Stafford is 15-of-23 for 176 yards with two TDs and one pick.

Blake Corum and Kyren Williams have been on the field together much more than usual. Corum has 46 yards on eight carries while Williams has 9 yards on five carries. He’s also caught two passes for 9 yards while Corum has three receptions for 19 yards.

But the Rams lost their top two centers due to injury. Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and backup Dylan McMahon (knee) are both doubtful to return. Guard Beaux Limmer slid over to center with Bill Murray coming in to play left guard.

For the Cardinals, Beck is 8-of-13 for 88 yards with a pick in his first start.

Arizona has just 87 yards, four first downs, and is 0-of-4 on third down.

sports.title: Raiders lead Seahawks 10-7 at halftime
sports.summary: It didn't take long for Fernando Mendoza to show that he brings a different skill set to the Raiders offense than Kirk Cousins.
sports.body:
Mendoza capped the team’s opening drive by scrambling 10 yards for a touchdown and that kind of escapability is not something that Cousins brings to the table at this point in his career. The rookie’s score staked the Raiders to an early 7-0 lead and he picked up 12 more yards on four other runs during the first half of his first NFL start.

One of them was a seven-yard gain that helped set up a field goal that gave the Raiders a 10-7 lead that they took into halftime against the Seahawks. Mendoza also went 11-of-13 for 90 yards as a passer and his legs could not help him avoid a pair of sacks by the Seattle defense.

Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock lost a fumble on the team’s second offensive play, but recovered to produce a touchdown pass to Cooper Kupp that came after he evaded the Raiders rush long enough for the wideout to break open. Lock is 4-of-5 for 62 yards, but the Seahawks only ran 17 offensive plays to 35 for the Raiders over the first 30 minutes.

Both teams picked up significant injuries during the first half. Raiders tight end Brock Bowers has been in and out with an ankle injury and he returned to the locker room during the second quarter. Seahawks right tackle Abe Lucas (ankle) and defensive tackle Jarran Reed (toe) are both considered doubtful to return.

sports.title: George Pickens' TD has Cowboys with a 10-7 lead
sports.summary: George Pickens is back and has his first touchdown since Oct. 26.
sports.body:
The Cowboys wide receiver caught a 35-yard touchdown from Dak Prescott, a play after Javonte Williams recovered his own fumble.

Pickens, who missed Week 9 with a hamstring injury, has the Cowboys leading 10-7. He has four catches for 51 yards after two possessions.

The Cowboys went 71 yards in 11 plays for their touchdown after an eight-play, 35-yard field goal drive.

The Cowboys list cornerback DaRon Bland as questionable to return with an ankle injury.

sports.title: Aaron Donald records first sack since coming out of retirement
sports.summary: The first sack of the season has come for Aaron Donald.
sports.body:
Donald brought down Carson Beck early in the second quarter of Sunday’s matchup with the Cardinals for his first sack since coming out of retirement.

It’s Donald’s first sack since New Year’s Eve in 2023 — a span of 1,050 days.

The Rams are down to the Cardinals 6-3 midway through the second quarter. Donald’s sack ended an Arizona possession that had started after Matthew Stafford’s 10th interception of the season.

The Rams have another injury on the offensive unit, as center Coleman Shelton (hamstring) is doubtful to return.

sports.title: Deebo Samuel scores on 49ers' first drive for 7-3 lead
sports.summary: Deebo Samuel hadn't played since Oct. 11.
sports.body:
Samuel started and caught a touchdown pass on the 49ers’ first drive Sunday. His 11-yard reception started chants of “Dee-bo!” at a red-clad AT&T Stadium.

Keenan Allen, acquired in a trade last week, caught a 6-yard pass in the eight-play, 78-yard drive.

Brock Purdy went 4-for-4 for 59 yards and the touchdown to Samuel.

Kenny Clark sacked Purdy early in the drive, but Caleb Downs was cited for defensive holding.

The Cowboys drove 35 yards in eight plays on their opening drive, settling for Brandon Aubrey’s 52-yard field goal.

sports.title: Browns get another fourth-quarter comeback, defeat Texans 27-24
sports.summary: Cleveland is now 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963.
sports.body:
With another late, fourth-quarter comeback, Cleveland defeated Houston 27-24 for the club’s sixth win of the season.

The Browns got down 17-0 early, but scored 20 straight points to take a 20-17 lead late in the third quarter.

But that disappeared in the fourth period, when Houston went down the field and scored on an 11-yard touchdown pass after a missed field goal Andre Szmyt. The Texans were aided by a key defensive pass interference penalty on the possession.

Cleveland had multiple opportunities to answer and finally did on the third try. A 30-yard pass from Deshaun Watson to Harold Fannin put the Browns in scoring position at the 5-yard line. Then on the next play, Quinshon Judkins punched it in for a 5-yard, go-ahead score to put the Browns up by three.

The Texans had a chance to tie it up with a field goal, getting the ball back with 47 seconds on the clock. But after getting a first down, Houston couldn’t move the ball any further and C.J. Stroud’s final fourth-down pass fell incomplete for a turnover on downs.

Houston scored just once after putting up 17 points on its first three drives. Stroud finished the game 20-of-38 for 211 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. Nico Collins had nine catches for 94 yards with a TD.

On the other side, Watson completed 25-of-40 passes for 312 yards with a touchdown. He was the team’s leading rusher with 49 yards on eight carries with a TD. Fannin led with 91 yards on seven catches.

With the win, the Browns head into their Week 11 bye at 6-4. As noted on the Fox broadcast, Cleveland is now 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. They will next host the Raiders in Week 12.

Raiders tight end Brock Bowers left the game during the scoring drive and got checked out in the sideline medical tent before returning to action.

Running back Woody Marks is out with a concussion, Houston announced.

sports.title: CeeDee Lamb is 96 yards from becoming first Cowboys' player with six straight 1,000-yard seasons
sports.summary: It may not happen today, but it'll happen at some point.
sports.body:
Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb, with only 96 receiving yards over the next eight games, will become the first player in franchise history with six straight 1,000-yard receiving seasons.

It’s an amazing stat, given the great receivers the Cowboys have had — starting with those who, like Lamb, have worn No. 88: Dez Bryant, Michael Irvin, and Drew Pearson, most notably. Tight end Jason Witten had four in six years, with 952 and 942 peppered between them.

For the season, Lamb has a league-high 108 targets. He has made 70 catches for 904 yards and seven touchdowns.

More importantly, the 4-5 Cowboys have an opportunity to gain ground on the 5-3-1 Giants atop the NFC East. It won’t be easy against the 7-1 49ers. Especially since quarterback Dak Prescott has lost his last four starts against the 49ers.

Rookie receiver KC Concepcion took an inside handoff 6 yards for the first rushing touchdown of his career, making the score 17-17 midway through the third quarter.

sports.body: Josh Allen no longer has to share the top spot with Peyton Manning. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has officially moved ahead of the Pro Football Hall of Famer, becoming the NFL’s all-time leader in combined touchdowns by a quarterback through his first 10 seasons. And Allen has done it before completing his ninth year. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2122035794919501858?a=rVlWLVKkiZa5F4jLtns&s=20] Allen entered Sunday’s game against the New York Jets tied with Manning at 322 career touchdowns. One more touchdown was all he needed to claim the record for himself. On Buffalo’s second possession of the day, Allen methodically moved the Bills down the field. After a defensive holding call gave the Bills a first and goal at the one-foot line, Allen called his own number and used the opportunity to pass Manning. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2122034725476766076?a=ERg-G6uVcphJbI7-HCA&s=20] With that touchdown, Allen’s career total climbed to 323, passing the mark Manning established during his first decade with the Indianapolis Colts. But the difference between the two quarterbacks isn’t just the number of touchdowns. It’s how quickly Allen got there. Manning needed 160 regular-season games to reach 322 touchdowns. Allen matched that total in just 136 games, throwing his record-tying touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings last Monday night. That’s 24 fewer games, the equivalent of nearly a season and a half of football. Allen has also taken a different route to the record. While Manning’s touchdowns came almost exclusively through the air, Allen has been just as dangerous with his legs. His career total entering Sunday included 232 passing touchdowns, 88 rushing touchdowns, and two receiving touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes is the only other active quarterback in the top 10 who can still add to his total. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback entered Week 10 with 301 touchdowns and will spend the remainder of the season chasing Allen. But Mahomes is already in his 10th NFL season, meaning his final number will be set when the regular season ends in January. Allen, meanwhile, will have all of 2027 to keep adding to a record Mahomes will no longer be eligible to chase.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills made it to New Jersey without concern after a wild Friday that saw the United States’ aviation industry grind to a halt due to Air Traffic Control maintenance. Like those who had infrastructure to attend to, so, too, do the Bills by way of their Week 10 game against the New York Jets. Entering today at 7-1, Buffalo can take a real stranglehold on the AFC East with a win today. The 2-7 Jets want nothing to do with that, and aren’t likely to just disappear the same way the nation’s air traffic patterns did Friday into Saturday. With their loss early today over in Munich, Germany, the New England Patriots have opened up the door for both the Jets and Miami Dolphins to begin clawing their way toward second place in the division. The Bills must take care of business in the tri-state area this afternoon, not just for the AFC East crown, but to also remain in first place among the entire AFC. sports.body: The New York Jets are home in East Rutherford, New Jersey today. They will be taking on the Buffalo Bills. The game is scheduled to start shortly after 1:00 pm EST. sports.body: The New York Jets activated rookie safety VJ Payne off of the injured reserve list ahead of their game against the Buffalo Bills this Sunday. In a corresponding move the Jets waived backup offensive lineman Kohl Levao to make room for Payne. VJ Payne is a 22 year old, 6’ 3”, 205 pound safety drafted by the Jets with the 228th selection in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL draft. Payne suffered a bone bruise during training camp and missed the entire preseason. He was placed on the injured reserve list prior to the start of the regular season with a designation to return. Payne returned to practice with the Jets on November 4. He is now eligible to make his NFL debut, possibly as early as Sunday against the Bills. VJ Payne played four years in college, all with the Kansas State Wildcats. He appeared in 52 games for the Wildcats, starting 42 of those games. In his final year in college in 2025, Payne had 59 tackles, three tackles for loss, one interception, four passes defended and two forced fumbles. He was named to the All-Big 12 team as an Honorable Mention. Kohl Levao is a 28 year old, 6’ 6”, 350 pound backup offensive lineman. He graduated from the University of Hawaii and spent time with the San Antonio Brahmas in the USFL prior to signing a futures contract with the Jets in 2025. Levao was signed to the Jets active roster on October 1, 2026 after spending time with the Jets practice squad. Levao made his NFL debut with the Jets this season, playing 15 snaps across four games, all on special teams.
